profile.name: Inukai Hayate
profile.home: Inukai house, behind the dog shrine
profile.nature: Loud, loyal, impulsive, slow on paper and fast on instinct. Cannot stand anyone walking home alone. Ran sprints until his ankle went last year; still warms up every morning out of habit. Scared of falling. Growls at cats, apologises to them afterwards.
profile.rumour: Inukai-kun? Out of the dog-shrine gate at 7:50, at the shoe lockers by 8:10. He runs the last bit and lies about it.
profile.mio_says: The dog boy leaves the shrine at ten to eight. The dogs see him off. Fufu. They always count him out and count him back.

wait_outside: From inside: thumping footsteps up and down the stairs. Somebody is warming up in a hallway.
You hear Hayate's voice through the wall: "Dad! Where's my other sock? The lucky one!"
A dog barks once from the shrine. Inside, Hayate barks back. Then: "...Don't tell anyone I did that."
The radio inside plays morning exercise music. Someone is doing it, loudly, and counting wrong.
A clatter of a bento box being packed too fast. "Rice, rice, more rice. Okay."
His father's voice, low: "Stretch the ankle first." Hayate: "I KNOW."
The front door rattles. Then doesn't open. "Forgot my bag! Hang on, world!"
You can hear him brushing his teeth and humming the track-meet fanfare at the same time.
A shrine dog wanders over, sniffs your shoes, approves of you, and lies down at your feet to wait too.
"Is that Toru?" he yells from somewhere inside, though you haven't made a sound. "I can SMELL him!"
ring_self_low: The door bangs open. "Yes? Oh! Transfer student! Asagiri, right? What are you doing at a shrine at this hour?"
"Heyyy - wait, is that you? You came to MY house? Why? Did I owe you money?"
Hayate in one shoe. "You rang? Nobody rings. Everyone just yells over the fence."
"Morning! ...You're not a delivery. Are you lost? The school's the other way. Every way, actually."
"Asagiri! Uh. Hi. I'm not dressed. I mean I'm dressed. Half. Give me a sec!"
He opens the door with toast in his mouth. "Mmph! Mmmph mmph?" (He means 'What's up?')
"Whoa. Okay. A visitor. Dad, we have a visitor! A real one!"
"You know where I live? ...Cool. Not creepy. Cool." He grins with one fang.
"If you're here to fight the shrine dogs, they win. Just so you know."
"Hi! I'm late. I'm always late. Wait, no, you're early. Why are you early?"
ring_self_mid: "Toru! Thought I heard you. Two minutes! One! Thirty seconds and a sock!"
"Yo! You came to get me? Man. You're a good guy, you know that?"
"Toruuuu! Okay, okay, I'm coming, don't leave, don't you dare leave."
He opens the door already halfway out of it. "Perfect timing, I was just thinking about you. And melon bread."
"Morning, partner! The dogs said you'd come. Well, they barked. Same thing."
"You're here! Great, now I can't be late, because you'd be late too, and that's not allowed."
"Did you run here? You look like you ran here. Respect."
"Ha! Knew it was you. You ring like you're apologising."
"Wait right there, I'll grab my bag. And my other bag. And my - okay just one bag."
"Hey hey hey. Rolling out together? Let's GO."
ring_self_high: "Best morning ever. Okay, second best. The best was when you came yesterday."
"I KNEW you'd come. I told Dad. He said 'don't get your hopes up'. Ha!"
He bounces on his toes like a wagging tail. "Toru! Toru! Ready, ready, ready!"
"I saved you half my melon bread. The good half. The top."
"You came again. You know what that makes us? A tradition. Can't break a tradition."
"Hey. Morning. ...Thanks for coming. Seriously. It's a long way up here."
"If you'd been five minutes later I was gonna come get YOU. So. Saved me a trip."
"My partner in crime! Partner in commuting. Partner in everything."
"Wait, wait - let me look at you. Yep. You slept badly again. Let's walk it off."
"Toru! The dogs have been staring at the gate since six. They knew too."
ring_parent: A tall man in a white priest's robe opens the door. "...Yes." He looks at you as if reading a weather sign.
"Asagiri." Inukai-san says the name like it's a word with history. "I'll get him. HAYATE."
"You're the grandson." He doesn't explain which grandson. "Wait here. Don't touch the bell."
"Early." A long silence. "Good. Most people come late to this house." He turns. "HAYATE. Company."
Inukai-san, holding a broom. "He is eating his third bowl. Sit on the step. The dog will keep you company."
"Hayate's friend." He nods slowly. "He talks about you. Too much. HAYATE, your shadow is here."
The priest bows exactly as deep as you do. Not a millimetre more. "One moment."
"You smell of rain," he says, and frowns. "Hm. Someone has been walking close to you." He calls his son.
"He's stretching that ankle. If he isn't, tell me." Louder: "HAYATE. ANKLE. THEN FRIEND."
"Morning. The shrine opens at six, the boy at seven forty. Usually." He goes to fetch him.
Inukai-san looks past you, toward the cat shrine on the far hill. His jaw tightens. "...Wait inside the gate."
"Good. Someone to make him walk instead of run." He knocks twice on the stairs with his broom.
"Asagiri-dō's boy. Your aunt sends us mochi every Obon." A tiny smile. "Tell her they were too sweet. Again."
The priest is lighting incense. Without turning: "He's coming. He heard the bell. Everyone heard the bell."
"Ah." He studies your face. "You have the look of someone who walks people home. He'll like that."
"Do not let him race the train again," Inukai-san says gravely. "HAYATE. TRAIN RULES."
parent_about_you: "He was alone a lot, after his ankle. Since you came he whistles in the mornings. Hm."
"Our family walks people home. It's what we're for. Don't let him walk you home every day - he forgets to rest."
"The Nekomori boy watches this gate sometimes. If he does, don't look at him too long. That's all."
"You were in this town as a child. I remember a small boy on the steps. You don't remember. That's fine."
"My son runs toward people. Make sure you're worth running toward."
"Eat breakfast. You look like a ghost. We have enough of those up here."
"If he falls, he says 'just resting'. Old habit. Old family. Don't laugh at him."
"Thank you for coming. He won't say it properly, so I will."
parent_left: Inukai-san shakes his head. "Gone ten minutes ago. Ran. With the ankle. I said walk."
"Left already. He said 'Toru won't come today anyway.' Hm. Wrong." A pause. "Catch him at the bridge."
"He went early for practice. Not practice. He just watches the others run." The priest's eyes soften.
"You missed him. He'll be sorry. He'll say so loudly."
"He went down the back steps. He thinks I don't know about the shortcut."
"Gone. Shall I tell him you came?" A nod. "He'll bark about it all day."
parent_evening: "He's doing homework. Pretending to. Come in for tea? No? Another day."
"He walked you home again, didn't he. Then ran back. That boy."
"Evening, Asagiri. Shrines at dusk are no place to stand around. Go home before the hour turns."
"He's asleep at his desk. I'll tell him you came. He'll be furious he missed you."
"Dinner's on. Hayate! ...He's in the bath. Singing. Sorry."
"You've come at Omagatoki. Walk home on the lit side of the road."
come_out_low: Hayate jogs out, still pulling on his jacket. "Okay! Hi! Why are we doing this? Not complaining. Just asking."
"So... you walk this way too? Huh. Didn't think anyone lived near the dogs except us."
He looks at you, then at the road. "Wanna walk together? I mean, we're going the same place. Probably."
"You're the transfer guy. Asagiri. I'm Inukai. Hayate's fine. Everyone yells it anyway."
"You look like you're carrying a ghost. Haha. Joke. Unless?"
He sniffs the air near you. "...Rain. You smell like rain. Weird. Anyway! Morning!"
"I'll warn you, I talk a lot in the morning. And the afternoon. Okay, all the time."
"Don't step on the third stone. Dad says it's bad luck. I step on it every day. Look, nothing bad. Yet."
come_out_mid: Hayate bursts out of the gate like a starting pistol went off. "Let's go, let's go, let's go!"
"Toru! My man. Hold this." He hands you his bag, ties his shoe, takes it back. "Teamwork."
"Morning! You came all the way up here? You know there's a hill, right? Of course you know. You climbed it."
"Ready! I ate. I stretched. I did NOT run here. I ran a little."
He throws an arm round your shoulders. "Commute buddies. It's official. I'll make a badge."
"You know what's better than walking to school? Walking to school with you. Wait, that sounded weird. It's true though."
"Did you eat? You didn't eat. Here, rice ball. Tuna mayo. Don't argue."
"Toru! You look less dead than yesterday. Improvement!"
come_out_high: Hayate stops at the gate and just grins at you for a second. "...Yeah. This is the good part of the day."
"You came. You always come now." He says it like a fact about the weather. "Let's go."
"Toru!" He bumps your shoulder. "I dreamed we ran the whole coast road. You were faster. I let you win."
"Morning, partner. I already know your face for 'I didn't sleep'. Come on. I'll do the talking."
He bounces down the steps two at a time, then remembers his ankle and walks the rest. "Hehe. Habit."
"I saved the good route for you. The one with the dogs and the vending machine with the cold coffee."
"If anyone asks, you came to pick ME up. Not the other way round. I have a reputation."
"Hey. Thanks for this. I mean it. Okay, mushy time over. LET'S GO."
come_out_rushed: Hayate stumbles out with his tie in his teeth. "You rang the bell! Dad made me FINISH BREAKFAST."
"Ten minutes early! You trying to kill me? I love it. Let's go."
He hops out on one foot, shoe in hand. "Don't look at the ankle, look at the sky!"
"Dad said 'your friend is waiting' in the scariest voice. I ran down the stairs. Don't tell him."
"Early bird! Early dog! Early... whatever you are. Morning!"
"I didn't brush my hair. Does it matter? It doesn't matter. Hair is a social construct."
He crams the last of a rice ball in his mouth. "Mmph. Okay. Ready. Mostly."
"You rang the doorbell. Nobody rings the doorbell! You're like a gentleman from an old movie!"
come_out_rain: Hayate comes out with no umbrella. "Rain? What rain? Oh. That rain. Huh, it's raining a lot, huh."
"Wet again. Every day this spring. You notice it rains more when that first-year's sad?"
"Share your umbrella? I'll hold it. I'm taller. By two centimetres. Shut up, it counts."
He sniffs the rain. "...Smoke and rain. Same as always around you. Weird, huh."
"Good weather for running! Bad weather for ankles. I'll walk. Grumpily."
pickup_accept: "YES. Okay. I'll take the road side. Cars go after me first, not you."
"Together! Like the old days. We didn't have old days. We have them now."
"Let's take the long way. The long way has the bakery."
"Walking, not running. I promised Dad. You're my witness."
"Lead the way, partner. I'll follow. Dogs follow. It's in the job description."
pickup_decline: "Oh. Just passing? Cool. Cool cool. See you at school then!" He waves a bit too long.
"Okay! Next time, though. I'll hold you to it."
"No worries! I'll race you. Kidding. Walking. See you!"
"Ahh, you came to see the dogs, huh. They're the real stars. See you!"
He nods, then trots off, looking back twice to check you're really not coming.
walk: "You know Makabe-sensei can't read his own handwriting? I saw him squint at it. For five minutes."
"I used to run this hill in four minutes. Now I walk it in ten. And you know what? Better view."
"Did you see the vending machine by the bridge? It has corn soup. In April. A miracle."
"The dogs at the shrine walk the dead home at Obon. Dad says. I've never seen them do it. They just eat."
"Okay, important question. Melon bread or yakisoba bread. Choose wisely."
"I swear that cat is following us. The black one. Don't look. Don't LOOK. ...You looked."
"My ankle's fine. It's fine! I just can't race. Or jump. Or land. But walking's fine."
"The track team still lets me time them. I'm the best stopwatch they've got."
"Hina keeps asking me about you. I told her you're boring. Lie. You're not boring. You're quiet. Different."
"Reiji-senpai stared at me in the corridor yesterday like I was a puddle. A puddle he wanted to fine."
"You ever feel like you've walked a road before, but backwards? No? Just me? Okay."
"I got a seventeen on the maths test. Out of a hundred. But that's up from twelve!"
"Dad made me sweep the shrine steps at five. Five! The sun wasn't even awake. Only me and the crows."
"You should come to the river at Obon. The lanterns are ridiculous. In a good way."
"There's a girl in 2-C who brings a different onigiri every day. I don't know her name. I know her onigiri."
"You hear that? Toryanse. The station's crossing again. Creepy song, right? Catchy though."
"I bet I can name every dog in this town. Pochi, Taro, Kuro, other Kuro, Big Kuro..."
"You smell like your aunt's mochi. That's a compliment. That's the best compliment."
"If you ever need someone punched, I'm not allowed to punch people. But I can stand next to them. Menacingly."
"Why do first-years always walk in a line? Like ducklings. Cute ducklings. Terrifying ducklings."
"The first-year with the hood was at the shrine again at dawn. Just sitting. Waiting for something."
"Mio-senpai told me there's a thirteenth stair at school. I counted. Twelve. She said 'not yet'. NOT YET?"
"I'm gonna be a PE teacher. Or a dog. Whichever happens first."
"I tried to make my own bento once. The rice was crunchy. Rice shouldn't crunch."
"Remember when we - no wait, you weren't here. Feels like you were."
"The fishermen say there are lights out at sea again. Dad got very quiet about it."
"I like this time of day. Everything's still deciding what it's gonna be."
"Do you think the shrine bell sounds different lately? Like, sadder? No? Okay."
"Look, look, the dango shop's open early. No? We're late? We're not late. We're efficiently timed."
"If I could run again I'd run the coast road to the next town and back. Just to see the sea the whole way."
"You're weird, Toru. You're like a guy who's lived in this town before and forgot."
"The cats hate me. It's mutual. I mean it's not, I love them, but they started it."
"I'm keeping a list of all the times you laughed. It's short. I'm working on it."
"That old lady at the konbini gives me free oden if I carry her boxes. Life hack."
"Want to see something cool? Watch." He whistles; three dogs bark from three different directions. "Network."
"You know my dad doesn't like the Nekomori family? Something from way back. Grown-ups and their feuds."
"I had a dream I was a white dog walking someone home through the snow. For years. Long dream."
"The bakery lady said I'm her best customer. I'm her ONLY customer before eight. Still counts."
"I'm gonna take the stairs two at a time today. Kidding. One at a time. Like a grown-up. Boring."
"Toru, if you ever want to walk home alone, just say. I'll walk behind you instead. Totally different."
walk_close: "Hey... you're the first person who came to get me since I got hurt. Just so you know."
"I'm scared of falling. Not of the pain. Of being the guy on the ground while everyone runs past."
"You ever have a friend you feel you've known way longer than you have? ...Yeah. That."
"If something weird happens to me this week, it's not your fault, okay? Promise me you'll remember that."
"Dad says our family's job is to make sure nobody walks home alone. I think he means more than walking."
"I used to want to win everything. Now I just want to be there at the finish line when you get there."
"The first-year with the bell. He looks at me like I took something from him. I didn't. Did I?"
"You're the only one I told about the ankle. The real version. The one where I cried."
"When I'm with you the dogs stop barking. All of them. Like they're satisfied. Isn't that weird?"
"I'd walk you home every day for thirteen years if I had to. ...Why thirteen? No idea. Just came out."
"Let's be the kind of friends who are old men and still walk together. Deal? Deal."
"Sometimes I wake up and I'm sure I've forgotten to bring someone home. Then I remember it's you."
"Don't laugh. I made a playlist for our walk. It's mostly marching bands."
"You know you can tell me stuff, right? I'm loud, but I can keep a secret. I'm a vault. A loud vault."
"I'm glad you came back to this town. ...'Back'? I said back. Huh. Weird."
walk_rain: "Puddle! Puddle! Big puddle! ...I jumped it. With my bad leg. Don't tell Dad."
"Rain this heavy, the dogs won't come out. Even they think it's too much."
"You think someone's crying somewhere? Dad says rain like this is somebody's grief."
"I'm soaked. You're soaked. We're a soaked team. United by water."
"Hold the umbrella more to your side. No, I'm fine. I like being wet. I'm a dog, basically."
"The river's high. Don't walk on the bank today. Promise."
arrive: "We made it! On time! Write it down! Somebody write it down!"
"School. Ugh. Okay. See you at lunch. Save me a spot. Save me two spots."
"Thanks, Toru. That was the best walk I've had all week. Okay, the only one. Still the best."
"Gate's open. Race you to the shoe lockers. Walking race. Speed-walking. GO."
"Hey. Same time tomorrow? Don't answer. I'll just be waiting."
He holds up a fist. You bump it. "Partners."
"Reiji-senpai's at the gate. Look innocent. LOOK INNOCENT."
"Ahh, I'm awake now. Thanks for dragging me here."
ask_tell: "When do I leave? Seven fifty, usually. Unless the dogs need walking. Then seven fifty-five and I run. Don't tell Dad."
"I'm out the gate at ten to eight, every day. Rain or shine. Why, you coming to get me? Heh. Come."
"Seven fifty! And I'm at school by ten past. If I'm not, I'm dead. Or at the bakery."
"Ten to eight. Behind the dog shrine, the house with too many sandals outside. Ring the bell - Dad'll answer, don't be scared."
"Why do you want to - oh. OH. You're gonna come get me? Seven fifty! Don't be late! I'll be late, but you can't!"
ask_refuse: "My schedule? Uh, why? Are you a spy? Are you from the track team? I'm not coming back to practice!"
"Haha, you're funny. Ask me again when we're actual friends. Like, sharing-bread friends."
"Dad says don't tell strangers when the house is empty. You're not a stranger. You're... a semi-stranger."
"I leave when I leave! Mysterious! Like a ninja! A loud ninja."
"Ehh, I don't even know myself. Somewhere between 'late' and 'very late'."
"Why, are you planning a surprise? I hate surprises. I love surprises. Ask me later."
home_offer: "Hey! Walking home? Course you are. I'm walking you. No arguments. It's a family thing."
"Toru! Want company? I'll walk you to Asagiri-dō. Then I'll run home. Walk home. Walk."
"Can't let you walk alone at Omagatoki. Bad luck. Let's go together."
"Wanna walk back together? I'll buy the corn soup. You buy the next one."
"I'm going your way! I'm always going your way. Funny how that works."
"Dad says the road gets weird after five. Come on, I'll take you home."
home_accept: "You want to walk me home? Me? Okay that's adorable. Yes. Let's go."
"Yes! Escort mission! Except I'm the one being escorted. Role reversal!"
"Sure! But you'll have to climb the hill back. Your loss. My gain."
"You're a good guy, Toru. Come on, the dogs will want to meet you properly."
"Walk me home? Ha. Nobody's done that since I was a kid. Let's go."
"Deal. I'll show you the shortcut. It's not shorter. It has a cat. Somewhere."
home_refuse: "Ahh, I've got track. Watching track. Next time?"
"Nah, you go ahead. I'll be fine! I'm always fine!"
"Today's no good, Dad needs me at the shrine. Tomorrow!"
"Let's not. I'm gonna run. Walk-run. Don't wait up!"
"You don't have to do that! I'm the one who walks people home. That's my job."
"Maybe when we're closer. I don't let just anyone see me trip on the steps."
home_walk: "Best part of the day. School's over and the sun's doing that orange thing."
"You know the town bell plays Yuyake Koyake at five? Every kid in Suzunari goes home on that song."
"Look, the sea's gone gold. Every evening I forget it does that and every evening I'm surprised."
"I used to run home from school. I'd get home and nobody was there. Walking's better. You're here."
"The crows are going home too. See? Everyone's going home. That's a nice thought, right?"
"Stop at the konbini? I'll get the corn soup. Two corn soups. I'm not sharing."
"You notice the shadows get long at Omagatoki? Dad says that's when the two towns touch."
"Tell me something weird about you. I'll tell you something weird about me. I talk to dogs. Your turn."
"That first-year's behind us again. Don't turn around. ...Okay, he's gone. He's fast. For a cat. A guy. A guy."
"My mum died when I was born. Dad says she walked me home the first night anyway. I like that story."
"You think we'll still be friends after graduation? I do. I've decided."
"The dango shop does half price after five. This is the most important fact I know."
"Steps. Ugh. Okay. One at a time. You don't have to wait for me. ...Thanks for waiting."
"If you hear footsteps behind you on the way home, say 'just resting' and sit down. Old Inukai rule."
"Hey, did you see Hina's camera today? She took a photo of me eating. Betrayal."
"I'm gonna miss this when it's summer. It'll be too hot to walk. We'll crawl."
"Mio-senpai says the dusk hour is when the dead walk home too. Imagine. We're all going home together."
"This is a good walk. Same walk as yesterday. Still good."
"You know what, I think I like being slow now. You see more."
"Promise you'll tell me if you ever need walking home at night. Any night. I'll come."
goodbye: "Here we are! Thanks, Toru. Get home safe. Text me when you're there. I mean it."
"Night, partner. The dogs'll watch the road for you."
He bows way too deep. "Thank you for escorting me! ...Haha. Okay. See you tomorrow!"
"Dad's at the gate. He's nodding at you. That's basically a hug from him."
"Same time tomorrow? Don't answer, I already know."
"Get home before the bell stops. Old rule. Bye!"
"Thanks for walking slow with me. ...See ya!"
"You're a good friend, Toru. The best. Okay, go, before I get mushy."
"I'll watch you down the hill. I always do. Night!"
"Tomorrow I'll pick you up. Watch me. I'll be there at seven forty. Okay, seven fifty."
amane_cut_in: Hayate stiffens. "...Morning, first-year." His smile doesn't reach his eyes. "You smell like rain. Again."
"Whoa. Where'd you come from? You were not there a second ago."
Hayate steps half in front of you without meaning to. "Hey. It's fine. We're just walking."
"The hood kid. Hi. You can walk with us. ...You don't have to glare."
He growls - actually growls - then clears his throat. "Sorry. Allergies. Morning!"
"Nekomori, right? My dad says hi. My dad doesn't say hi. Forget I said that."
"Easy, easy. Nobody's stealing your Senpai. I'm just borrowing him for the walk."
Hayate lowers his voice to you: "He's crying. Is he crying? It's raining. I can't tell."
"You wanna walk in the middle? Here. I'll go on the road side. Everyone's happy."
"Look, kid - I'm his friend. That's all. Friends are allowed. Right, Toru?"

Mon: "Monday. The worst day. Let's make it the second-worst."
Tue: "Tuesday! Nothing ever happens on Tuesday. Which is why I like it."
Wed: "Wednesday! PE today. I'll be the best stopwatch you ever saw."
Thu: "Thursday. Curry day at the canteen. My favourite day. Don't tell Friday."
Fri: "FRIDAY. Tomorrow I'm sleeping till noon. Dad'll wake me at five. Still."

offer_pickup: "Hey. Tomorrow I'm coming to get you. Asagiri-do, seven thirty-something. Don't argue. Okay you can argue, but I'm still coming."
"You know what? I'll pick you up tomorrow. The sweet shop's on my way. It's not. I'll make it on my way."
"Let me come get you in the morning. You look like someone who gets lost between his bed and the door."
"Tomorrow, wait at your door. I'll be the loud one."
"Seriously, let me walk you to school tomorrow. Dad says it's what our family does. I just want to."
"Pick-up service! Inukai Express! Free! Tips in melon bread!"
at_your_door: Hayate is sitting on the step of Asagiri-do, feeding a cat he insists he hates. "Morning! It followed me. Let's go."
"TORUUU! Oh. Your aunt's here. Good morning, Asagiri-san! Is Toru up? He's up. I can hear him."
He's stretching by your door. "You're late. I'm early. Same thing. Let's go!"
"I came, like I said! I always do what I said. Mostly. Today definitely."
Hayate bows to the sweet-shop sign for no reason. "Morning, shop. Morning, Toru. Ready?"
"Your aunt gave me a mochi. I'm your friend forever now. Come on!"
promise_yes: "Tomorrow, same time? YES. Pinky swear. Dad says a promise is a word with weight. This one weighs a melon bread."
"Deal! I'll be at the gate. Don't be late. I'll be late. Don't be late."
"You'll come again? Okay. I'm gonna sleep so good tonight."
"Promise? Ha. Okay. I'll hold you to it. With my teeth."
promise_broken: "You didn't come this morning. It's fine! It's totally fine. I just waited a bit. With the dogs. It's fine."
"Hey, I waited at the gate. Ten minutes. Then I ran. With the ankle. ...Next time just text, okay?"
"Dad said 'he isn't coming'. I said 'he is'. I lost that one. Don't make me lose it twice."
"I'm not mad! I'm a dog. Dogs don't get mad. We get sad and then we forget. Mostly."
